{"payload": {"memory_citation": null, "message": "To make it non-fluff, define “intelligence” as measurable closed-loop capability:

```text
Given a repo, task, tests, logs, and constraints,
the model chooses actions that increase verified progress under budget.
```

So you do not train “intelligence” directly. You train the loop that produces it:

```text
observe repo state
choose next action
emit valid code or command
run verifier
read failure
choose repair / test / abstain
repeat
```

For our model, the real training target should become:

```text
state -> action -> verified outcome
```

Not just:

```text
prompt -> expected text
```

The concrete path:

1. Fix valid emission first

If it cannot emit valid code reliably, nothing downstream matters. Prefix parity, schema parity, target formatting, tokenizer behavior, and decoder surface need to be locked down.

Training objective:

```text
repo/task context -> syntactically valid, localized, executable code patch
```

Metrics:

```text
parse valid
imports valid
compiles
unit test runnable
patch applies
no malformed output
```

2. Add verifier-labeled outcomes

Every candidate should become training data with outcome labels:

```text
patch compiled: yes/no
tests passed: yes/no
failure type
error span
repair needed
should abstain
should add test
should inspect file
```

This turns raw generation into software-development feedback.
